_note: Draft English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Bereshit 44 (the silver cup; Judah's plea). Saadia-specific: v.5 'אנמא אמתחנכם בה' = 'he tests by it' (substitutes for נחש 'divines' — anti-magical); v.7 'מעאד'ין' = 'far be it from us' (consistent with B18:25 idiom).

translations.1: Then he commanded his steward, and said: 'Fill the sacks of the people with food, as much as they can carry; and set each man's silver in the mouth of his sack.
translations.2: And place my goblet — the silver goblet — in the mouth of the sack of the youngest, with the silver for his grain.' And he did as Joseph had said to him.
translations.3: And when the morning was light, the men were sent away, they and their donkeys.
translations.4: They had gone out of the city, and had not gone far, when Joseph said to his steward: 'Arise, pursue after the men; and when you overtake them, say to them, "Why have you repaid evil for good?
translations.5: Is not this the one from which my lord drinks, and by which he tests? You have done evil in what you have done."'
translations.6: And he overtook them, and spoke to them with these words.
translations.7: They said to him: 'Let my lord not say these words. Far be it from your servants from doing such a thing.
translations.8: Behold, the silver which we found in the mouths of our sacks — we returned to you from the land of Canaan. How then should we steal silver or gold from your master's house?
translations.9: Whoever of your servants it is found with — let him die; and we also shall be slaves to my lord.'
translations.10: He said: 'Now, as you have said, so let it be — the one with whom it is found shall be my slave; and the rest of you shall be innocent.'
translations.11: And they hurried, and each man laid his sack upon the earth; and each man opened his sack.
translations.12: And he searched — beginning with the eldest and ending with the youngest; and he found the goblet in Benjamin's sack.
translations.13: And they tore their garments, and each man loaded his donkey, and they returned to the city.
translations.14: And Judah and his brothers came to Joseph's house — and he was still there — and they fell down before him upon the earth.
translations.15: Joseph said to them: 'What deed is this that you have done? Did you not know that a man like me tests?'
translations.16: Judah said: 'What shall we say to my lord? What shall we speak, and how shall we plead? God has caught out your servants in their offense. Here we are slaves to my lord — we, and the one in whose hand the goblet was found.'
translations.17: He said: 'Far be it from me from doing this thing. The man in whose hand the goblet was found — he shall be my slave; and as for you, go up in peace to your father.'
translations.18: Then Judah drew near to him and said: 'O my lord, let your servant speak a word in the presence of my lord; and let not your anger flare against your servant — for you are like Pharaoh.
translations.19: Did my lord ask his servants, saying, "Have you a father or a brother?"
translations.20: And we said to my lord, "We have an aged father, and a child of his old age, a young one; and his brother is dead; and he alone is left of his mother — and his father loves him."
translations.21: And you said to your servants, "Bring him down to me, that I may set my attention upon him."
translations.22: And we said to my lord, "The boy cannot leave his father; if he should leave him, he would die."
translations.23: And you said to your servants, "If your youngest brother does not come down with you, you shall not see my face again."
translations.24: And when we went up to your servant our father, we told him the words of my lord.
translations.25: And our father said, "Return, buy us a little food."
translations.26: We said, "We cannot go down; only if our youngest brother is with us shall we go down; for we cannot see the face of the man unless our youngest brother is with us."
translations.27: And your servant our father said to us, "You know that my wife bore me only two sons.
translations.28: And the one of them went out from me, and I said, perhaps he has been torn — and I have not seen him until now.
translations.29: And if you take this one also from me, and calamity befalls him, you would bring down my old age with sorrow to the dust."
translations.31: And it shall be — when he sees that the boy is not with us — he shall die; and your servants shall have brought down the old age of your servant our father with sorrow to the dust.
translations.32: For your servant became surety for the boy with my father, saying, "If I do not bring him back to you, I shall be at fault before my father all my days."
translations.33: Now therefore — let your servant remain in place of the boy, as a slave to my lord; and let the boy go up with his brothers.
translations.34: For how shall I go up to my father — and the boy is not with me — lest I see the calamity that would befall him?
translations.36: I am afraid that, when I come to your servant my father, and the boy is not with us — and his soul is bound to his soul —'
